transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-22 11:00am PT | Duration: ~58m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Alex (ScoutLabs CTO), Priya (ML Eng), Sam (Platform)

Auto-summary (auto-gen):
- Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a document-retrieval product with PHI-ish telemetry; strong interest in Dedicated for predictable latency and Private for compliance gating.
- Integration concerns: LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, SDKs for Go/Node/Python, gateway/proxy pattern, per-route quotas/rate limits, observability hooks (OpenTelemetry, traces, per-request metadata).
- Next actions: benchmarks, security pack, pilot kickoff.

[00:00] Maya: "All right thanks everyone for joining. Quick intro from us: I'm Maya, AE, and Ethan is our SE — we'll kick off with 10 minutes on your stack then dig into the integration concerns. Alex, want to start with a short context on what ScoutLabs is trying to build?"

[00:18] Alex: "Yeah thanks. So ScoutLabs does realtime incident summarization for our mobile CRM product. We're ingesting chat logs, call transcripts, customer records — some of that is sensitive. We're prototyping an assistant that does retrieval-augmented generation, with LangChain currently in our pipeline. Chief concerns are latency under load, cost per 1k tokens, and keeping the PII / PHI inside our VPC. That's why we reached out — wanted to understand Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs."

[00:45] Ethan: "Great. We'll try to map out where each deployment mode fits. For Hosted you get fastest onboarding but data residency and retention controls are limited to our hosted policy. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and isolation — you can pin model variants. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you a private control plane and full network isolation, plus KMS integration. A lot of customers start Hosted then move to Dedicated or Private as they hit compliance and SLO thresholds."

[01:12] Priya: "We plan to use LangChain for orchestration and LlamaIndex for some vector store glue. Is there an existing adapter for LlamaIndex or do we need to write a connector? Also, we use Go for the proxy layer and Node for edge functions — SDK support?"

[01:30] Ethan: "We have first-class SDKs for Python, Node, and Go. The Go SDK has most of the features for request streaming and metadata. For LangChain we provide a simple wrapper and many customers use the LangChain LLM wrappers — we also have a maintained example repo. For LlamaIndex, there's not a vendor-specific plugin bundled, but it's fairly straightforward: you can use our REST endpoints or SDK from within LlamaIndex's runtime. We'll share a quickstart snippet.

(implicit transcription: link mentioned) redwood integration quickstart: https://redwood.ai/integration-guide (note: internal link)"

[02:05] Sam: "On the network side, if we go Private we need to know the VPC peering setup, egress rules, and whether the runtime needs outbound internet access. Also, cert/key management — we use AWS KMS and an HSM for some keys. Does Redwood support bringing your own KMS/HSM?"

[02:28] Maya: "Yes, for Private we support customer-managed KMS. We can also run in an on-prem package for air-gapped cases — that's heavier ops but doable. We'll include KMS/HSM integration details in the security pack I'll send. For Dedicated you can also set KMS to your account depending on the cloud provider and contract."

[02:50] Alex: "Latency — our SLAs are tight: p95 under 350ms for 256-token responses. Can Dedicated meet that with our expected QPS? What about batching — do we lose latency?"

[03:06] Ethan: "Good question — Dedicated is tuned for predictable throughput. We support continuous batching; you can configure max batch latency and max batch size. For low-latency tails customers use smaller batch windows or enable isolation policies so some instances prioritize low-latency requests. We can run benchmarks with your seq-len distribution. Typical numbers we've seen for similar models: p95 in the 200–400ms range with batching tuned for latency. We'll run a 512-token baseline for you.

[03:38] Priya: "About quotas and rate limits: we have a multi-tenant gateway where internal teams call the Redwood endpoint. Need per-route quotas (per-team), token quotas, and burst limits. Also want to be able to configure a fallback model for high-cost calls. How granular are your rate-limit controls?"

[03:58] Ethan: "We expose per-key and per-route quotas; the Console lets you configure token quotas, QPS caps, and burst windows. There's also routing policies — you can route lower-tier traffic to cheaper model variants automatically. We also support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. For proxy patterns, many customers put a lightweight gateway (sidecar or central API gateway) in front of Redwood to enforce auth and quotas, but you can also leverage our built-in rate limiting if you want centralized control."

[04:28] Sam: "We prefer the gateway to be in our infra for auditability. Want to keep an audit trail of request IDs that tie back to our traces (OpenTelemetry). Do we get trace propagation and per-request metadata back from Redwood?"

[04:40] Maya: "Yes — we have observability hooks. You can pass request metadata headers; Redwood emits traces and spans that can be correlated via request-id. We also support OpenTelemetry export so you can ingest into your tracing backend. Console will show per-route latency and token breakdowns. We'll share the tracing integration doc."

[05:00] Priya: "Streaming: we do partial token rendering in the UI. Does the Node SDK support server-sent events / streaming websocket? We need to push partial responses back to clients as they're generated."

[05:12] Ethan: "Node SDK supports streaming via EventSource and websockets; Python and Go have streaming primitives as well. For Private deployments we also support streaming over internal network. There are some proxy timeouts to be aware of — we'll document recommended keepalive and chunk sizes for the gateway."

[05:32] Alex: "Cost model — per-token plus embedding costs, right? We need to estimate monthly cost at ~150M tokens. How do Dedicated/Private pricing differ?"

[05:43] Maya: "Hosted is usage-based per token/embedding. Dedicated is reserved capacity — you commit to a monthly GPU pool and get a reduced per-token effective cost plus predictable throughput. Private has a platform licensing fee plus support; exact economics depend on ops footprint. We'll send a pricing matrix comparing typical numbers for your throughput profile. Also, Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and quantization profiles to reduce unit cost."

[06:10] Sam: "About caching: we have a lot of repeated prefixes for templated responses. Can Redwood do prefix caching or KV cache at the platform so we don't pay for repeated tokens?"

[06:20] Ethan: "Yes — we do automatic prefix caching and support KV cache management to reduce token usage where appropriate. It's workload dependent but provides big wins in chat-like workloads. You can configure TTLs and invalidation behavior. We'll share a case study for caching gains."

[06:40] Priya: "On the LangChain/LlamaIndex side: we want the retriever to call Redwood embeddings for vector store creation and then the generator to use cached context up to a window. Any recomended patterns?"

[06:52] Ethan: "Common pattern: do embeddings in a batched background job (e.g., 4–8 per request) and store vectors in your vector DB (we integrate with common stores). For the generator, use a Retriever that assembles top-k documents and then use Redwood's structured output to ask for JSON. Note, for long context you can use KV cache and cache the KV for frequent users — reduces compute. We'll share a sample LangChain pipeline (we have a 'recipes' repo)."

[07:18] Alex: "Security questions: SOC2, ISO? Audit logs? We need to show security to legal. Also, what about data deletion and retention?"

[07:28] Maya: "We are SOC2 compliant; our security pack has ISO notes, audit log format, and data retention settings. For Hosted you can request shorter retention windows; Dedicated and Private give you more control. For Private we can also offer an on-prem pattern where data never leaves your network. We'll attach the security pack to the follow-up."

[07:45] Priya: "Edge case: if model fails or capacity is constrained, can we fallback to a smaller model automatically? We want graceful degradation not 500s."

[07:55] Ethan: "Yes — Smart routing allows fallbacks to compatible model variants by policy. You can also set a priority order for model variants and regions. We expose status hooks so your gateway can detect degradation and route accordingly."

[08:15] Sam: "Operationally, who owns runtime upgrades? If we go Dedicated or Private, how are model updates handled?"

[08:25] Maya: "For Dedicated we manage the runtime but upgrades are controlled by deployment windows you approve. For Private we can offer a managed private control plane or hand off upgrades; it's configurable per contract. Rollouts include canary and automatic rollback on regressions. Redwood Optimize and our eval hooks help detect quality regressions based on your test prompts."

[08:48] Alex: "One more: network egress / data residency — some customers require EU-only. Do you have region pinning for Hosted?"

[08:56] Ethan: "Yes we have region pinning for Hosted; Dedicated and Private can be deployed in target regions. We'll document the region coverage matrix."

[09:10] Maya: "Ok wrapping: quick recap of things we'll send — security pack (SOC2/KMS/HSM notes), SDK quickstarts (Go/Node/Python), LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter examples, benchmark plan and pricing matrix. Pilot kickoff week of 11/29 pending Alex confirmation. Anything else to call out?"

[09:30] Alex: "Please include a sample gateway config for rate limits and OpenTelemetry headers so Sam can start mapping to our infra. Also include recommended keepalive settings for streaming. That'll help us size and plan firewall windows."

[09:45] Priya: "And sample LangChain retriever code with the expected latencies so we can budget the user-perceived latency in the UI."

[09:56] Maya: "Will do. Ethan — you're running the benchmark?"

[10:00] Ethan: "Yep, I'll run Dedicated baseline (512 tokens) and share perf + cost spreadsheet. I'll also include a smaller Hosted run for comparison. I'll upload to the shared folder: https://drive.company/scoutlabs/redwood-benchmarks (note: placeholder)."

[10:15] Alex: "Great, thanks. We'll reconvene after the benchmark and security review. If all good we'll sign the SOW for Dedicated pilot."

[10:25] Maya: "Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with the pack and links by EOD Tuesday. Meeting adjourned."

(end of transcript)
